description: Send a batch of plain-text emails from the connected Gmail account. Each message needs at least one "to" address, a subject, and a body. Every message reports its own outcome: results[i].ok tells you whether message i went out, with the new message id when it did and the reason when it did not.

subject.description: One line. A line break here would be header injection, so it is refused.

header_safe_address.description: An email address, optionally with a display name. A bare newline is the whole of RFC 2822 header injection - it ends the header and lets the rest of the string write its own Bcc - so the pattern refuses one.

response_schema.description: Lenient ingress on the Message resource users.messages.send answers with. Open on purpose: Gmail adds fields and a closed schema would turn that into an outage.

quirks.no_batch_endpoint: Gmail has no batch send - users.messages.send takes one message - so the plural contract runs through fan_out: bounded concurrent singles under the app's rate limits, one result per message, in the caller's order.
quirks.not_atomic: Sending is deliberately not atomic. Three mails going out and one bouncing is three mails delivered, and the caller is told exactly which one failed.
quirks.raw_message: users.messages.send takes exactly one field: raw, an RFC 2822 message in base64url. Gmail writes no headers for you, so execute.ts writes the email itself.
quirks.encoding: The body travels as base64 with 76-character lines: RFC 2045 caps an encoded line at 76 and RFC 2822 rejects any line over 998, and base64 keeps a UTF-8 body intact where raw 8-bit text does not. A subject with an accent or an emoji travels as an RFC 2047 encoded word.
quirks.header_injection: to, cc and subject must not contain CR or LF. The input_schema patterns refuse it and execute.ts checks again, because a header break is a trust boundary and not a formatting preference.
